title: Words that follow the parameter

steps.say: Type the region into the title and render for Riyadh: the summary says Riyadh, the title still says Jazan.
Inline R works in the header too: knitr reads the whole file, header included. Only a file with no R chunk skips knitr and prints the code as text.
The hard part: a sentence that makes a claim must come from a rule. case_when() states the threshold and all three outcomes. Riyadh fell, Jazan rose; neither word is typed.

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tinytable)
rates <- read_csv("unemployment.csv")
REGION <- params$region
now <- rates |>
  filter(region == REGION, quarter == "2025Q4") |>
  pull(rate)
then <- rates |>
  filter(region == REGION, quarter == "2022Q1") |>
  pull(rate)
trend <- case_when(
  now - then > 0.5 ~ "rose",
  now - then < -0.5 ~ "fell",
  .default = "barely moved"
)
```

## Summary

::: {.column-margin}
Rates are a share of the labour force, in %.
:::

Unemployment **fell** in most regions between 2022 and 2025.
*Jazan* is the exception. This note shows the national
trend (@fig-trend) and the latest rates
(@tbl-latest).[^1]

Unemployment in `r REGION` `r trend` between 2022 and 2025.
In `r REGION` the rate was
`r scales::number(now, accuracy = 0.1)`% in 2025 Q4,
against `r scales::number(then, accuracy = 0.1)`% in
2022 Q1: a change of
`r scales::number(now - then, accuracy = 0.1, style_positive = "plus")`
points.

The data cover:

- 13 regions and the Kingdom as a whole
- 16 quarters, from 2022 Q1 to 2025 Q4

@sec-method defines the rate.

Official figures are on the [GASTAT website](https://www.stats.gov.sa).

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
::: {.callout-tip}
This page is updated every quarter. Bookmark it.
:::
:::

::: {.content-visible unless-format="html"}
Printed `r format(Sys.Date(), "%d %B %Y")`. The latest version is online.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="docx"}
**Reviewer:** check the Jazan figures against the Q4 file.
:::

[^1]: All figures in this note are synthetic, made for training.

## Method {#sec-method}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How the rate is defined"}
The unemployment rate is

$$
u = \frac{U}{U + E} \times 100
$$

where $U$ is the number unemployed and $E$ the number employed.
:::


## Latest rates

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Table

```{r}
#| label: tbl-latest
#| tbl-cap: "Unemployment rate by region, 2025 Q4 (%)"
latest <- rates |> filter(quarter == "2025Q4")
latest |>
  arrange(rate) |>
  select(Region = region, `Rate (%)` = rate) |>
  tt() |>
  format_tt(digits = 1, num_fmt = "decimal",
            num_zero = TRUE) |>
  theme_html(portable = TRUE)
```

### Chart

```{r}
latest |>
  ggplot(aes(rate, fct_reorder(region, rate))) +
  geom_col() + labs(x = "Rate (%)", y = NULL)
```
:::
